title: Best practices and troubleshooting
summary: Keep scene code predictable by making timing, ownership, geometry updates and rendering intent explicit.

items: Introduce the subject before changing it; use transforms to preserve identity.
Keep colors consistent with semantic roles across formula, geometry and labels.
Use measured bounds and explicit camera framing after content is ready.
Inspect intermediate morph frames and readable typography at final output size.
Keep a brief final hold long enough for the viewer to understand the result.
Reuse entity instances and typed-array capacities for continuous updates.
Change shader parameters without rebuilding shader topology where possible.
Use GPU instancing for repeated compatible geometry and CPU entities for heterogeneous behavior.
Measure analytical versus fast paths with the actual view and effects.
Reduce SSAA, shadow, transparency and tracing cost independently while diagnosing a bottleneck.
Do not add per-frame GPU readbacks unless the application really needs CPU access to the result.
Check canvas dimensions and navigator.gpu/adapter availability.
Open the console and distinguish asset fetch errors from WebGPU validation errors.
Verify the default Scene export and await composer initialization before GPU work.
Draw one simple primitive with an explicit camera before loading a large model.
Check VISIBILITY, alpha, layer masks, camera position and empty bounds.
Check that geometry is attached once and that a matching renderer/fragment component exists.

blocks.text: Diagnose frozen updates or bad timing

An always callback is not a wall-clock interval. Keep the composer in continuous mode for a continuously moving simulation, or ensure active animations/invalidation cause frames. Use `(time, dt)` in that order and convert milliseconds to seconds for a physical solver. Check await on play/wait and avoid an infinite animation in a sequence that must reach later steps.

When a seek differs from a fresh render, look for Date.now, performance.now, network completion, mutable external state and unseeded randomness. Snapshots of engine State cannot automatically restore every custom JavaScript variable or third-party solver state.
